answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a separate bond before bidding on paid tasks, whether drafting a sonnet, inspecting a bridge, or mapping a glacier. Bonds stay locked through a dispute window and are slashed for provable fraud, with no extra bidding power granted to unbonded accounts. An attacker can create endless names, but running 1,000 eligible identities requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and risking its loss.
